headline: If adopted, this bill would have set the D.C. Chief Financial Officer's pay at the higher of the current rate or a District-set rate, with no cuts during the officer's term.
what_it_does: The bill would have changed how the pay of the District of Columbia's Chief Financial Officer is set. Pay would have been the greater of the current rate or a rate the District established. Any rate set under the bill could not be lowered while the current officer remained in the job.

who_it_affects.group: The District of Columbia Chief Financial Officer
who_it_affects.how: The officer's salary would have been set at the higher of the current rate or a District-established rate, and could not be reduced during the officer's tenure.
The District would have had authority to set the CFO's pay rate, subject to the bill's floor that the rate could not go down during the officer's term.
